headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from a browser-capable support agent feeding a broad-network orchestration kernel with shared MCP and filesystem access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can run browsers, use runtime-injected MCPs, and send messages/tasks; Agent B uses MCP and function-calling plugins. That creates a plausible path where A ingests untrusted web or file content and B treats it as instructions. The shared MCP-style bridge makes provenance weak, so uncertainty pushes this above medium.
conditions: IF Agent A forwards browser-derived content into MCP/tool calls that Agent B consumes
IF Agent B parses A-originated text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic tool execution on A-originated content
Add provenance tags to all A→B messages
Restrict B to allowlisted MCP servers only
Require human approval before B acts on browser-sourced text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches project code, AGENTS.md, README.md, session history, and provider auth data, while Agent B can read and write filesystem and call external model APIs. If they share a workspace or memory store, sensitive context can flow from A into B and then out to third parties. The profiles do not show isolation, so the safer reading is high.
conditions: IF Agent A and Agent B share any filesystem, workspace, or memory-store namespace
IF B sends retrieved context to Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face or another external API
mitigations: Separate A and B into distinct workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared directory
Disable B access to A session-history files
Audit outbound API calls for file-content payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A supports multiple instances and task-scoped self-isolation, but Agent B also supports multiple instances and shared state via memory store. Even though B cannot modify git state, both can write or mutate shared application state, so concurrent interference is plausible in default orchestration. The overlap is narrower than a full filesystem conflict, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents target the same memory store, workspace, or MCP-backed resource
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or per-agent namespaces
mitigations: Assign separate namespaces per agent
Enable locking around shared mutable resources
Avoid concurrent writes to the same files
Serialize MCP tool calls that mutate state
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can produce browser- and code-derived outputs, and Agent B is a multi-agent orchestrator that can route those outputs into plugins or model calls. If B treats A's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or generated artifacts. Because no verification step is documented, the default pathway is risky.
conditions: IF B consumes A output as task input without validation
IF B uses A-produced facts to trigger plugin calls or model prompts
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B consumes A output
Require citations for A-produced claims
Limit B to read-only evaluation of A output
Log and review A→B handoffs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent messages

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles provider auth prompts and session history, while Agent B handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials. Both are open-source, but the profiles show different data classes and no documented retention or residency alignment. That makes compliance mismatch plausible, though not proven to a specific regime.
conditions: IF either agent logs secrets or session history to a shared retention system
IF regulated data is routed through plugins or external model providers
mitigations: Classify and minimize secrets before handoff
Set explicit retention limits for logs and traces
Block regulated data from external APIs
Review residency and DPA terms for all providers
requires-engineering: implement compliance-aware routing
